observation.visible_scene: A single crescent-shaped watermelon wedge sits centered on a plain, evenly lit off-white surface. The cut face shows red flesh with embedded pale seeds, a glossy wet patch on the left side, a pale yellow inner rind, and a thin green outer rim. Static overlays are present: a 'Day 1 / Hour N' clock at bottom-left, a temperature/RH readout at top-right, and a circular 't²' logo at bottom-right. The clip is a time-lapse segment of this slice.
visible_changes: The on-screen clock advances continuously from Day 1 Hour 29 to Hour 36.
The temperature label steps from 32°C/89°F to 31°C/87°F partway through; the RH label fluctuates (47% → 52–55% → 50–47%) rather than changing monotonically.
The red cut surface gradually loses its glossy wet sheen and looks more matte and grainy, most noticeably on the left portion, with the red appearing slightly duller by the end.
The pale rind along the bottom edge develops more yellowish/mottled patches over the segment.
A small dark bead of juice appears at the lower-right edge of the rind around the middle of the clip and remains visible to the last frame.
The slice's position, orientation, and outline stay essentially fixed, and the background and logo do not move, indicating a static camera and no object translation or rotation.
outside_clip_unknowns: The decay/drying process was already underway before Hour 29 and continues after Hour 36; later outcomes (heavy drying, mold, structural collapse) are not shown.
The mechanism producing the juice bead (seepage vs. condensation) and its ultimate fate (drip, evaporation) are not visible.
Whether the recorded temperature/humidity changes drive the visual drying or merely co-occur cannot be determined from the frames.
uncertain_details: The precise frame at which the juice bead first forms, and whether it grows or stays constant, is hard to pin down.
Subtle shifts in flesh color/texture could partly reflect lighting or compression rather than physical change.
The RH trend direction is ambiguous because the values rise and fall non-monotonically.
